scores.label: A
scores.note: 1: 'their posts' misreads whose posts, and it drops the comparison and 'all day'. 2 and 4: drop the posts and 'all day', which link the sentence to the paragraph, and 'compare to others' lacks 'themselves'. 3 and 5: drop the comparison, which is the key mechanism, and 'all day'. 5 also drops 'about their lives'.

scores.label: B
scores.note: Every option keeps the posts and the constant viewing. 3 is the cleanest and most precise ('feelings of inadequacy'). 1, 2 and 4 replace 'feel bad' with 'compare negatively/unfavorably'. 5 keeps every detail but is wordy. 2/5 and 1/4 are close to each other.

scores.label: C
scores.note: 1-4 all drop the posts and 'all day', which link the sentence to the paragraph. 2-4 also drop who is comparing and what with, so they are too thin for the essay. They are near copies of each other. Option 5 failed the code check and was not judged.

scores.label: D
scores.note: 5: 'daily' changes 'all day' and weakens the claim. 4 is clean and keeps the meaning. 1-3 are correct but plain or awkwardly ordered. All of them drop 'about their own lives'.

scores.label: E
scores.note: 2: drops 'all day', and 'self-compare' and 'feel discontent' read oddly. 4: 'daily' changes 'all day', 'edited' adds a claim, and the comparison is dropped. 5: 'frequent' weakens 'all day', the comparison is dropped, and 'feel less about themselves' is unidiomatic. 1: 'compare' has no object. 3: 'highlight reels' is a metaphor that may confuse readers.
